column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the first object unnamed and calls earth’s ends wings; BSB explicitly names lightning and the ends of the earth.
The Hebrew uses a plural them for what He does not restrain; BSB explicitly identifies lightning.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats a shower of rain and does not separately call the first rain gentle; BSB contrasts gentle rain and mighty downpour.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has a singular animal; BSB has plural wild animals.
The Hebrew does not separately express north in the second phrase; BSB specifies north winds.
The Hebrew describes the water’s breadth as constrained; BSB says the expanses are frozen.
The Hebrew names the cloud of His light as what He scatters; BSB describes scattering lightning through the clouds.
The Hebrew first has a singular it; BSB starts with plural they.
The Hebrew lists punishment, His land, and loving devotion as alternatives; BSB makes loving devotion the manner of accomplishing the other two.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names the light of His cloud; BSB identifies lightning.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says with Him and hard like a cast mirror without explicitly naming heat or bronze; BSB says like Him and adds reflecting heat and bronze.
The Hebrew gives darkness as the reason without explicitly naming faces; BSB adds faces in darkness.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names light and says people do not see it; BSB identifies the sun and describes inability to gaze at it.
The Hebrew makes gold the subject that comes from the north; BSB describes Him coming in golden splendor.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says He does not see or regard the wise in heart; BSB interprets this as no partiality.
